observed.source: Codex session rollout (CLI-recorded thread settings; not model-authored)

result.decision_rationale:
All four prior fixes are verified. One status defect remains. After an amendment retires a verdict or handoff receipt, the controller can keep reporting that publication as pending indefinitely.

Continuation for Claude

Correct the `pending_publications` filter so it reports work awaiting delivery or reconciliation. A superseded record with a settled delivery outcome should drop out of the list. Keep the change confined to status reporting and its tests. Extend the two existing rejected-POST amendment fixtures to check the retired keys, preserve visibility of genuinely uncertain delivery, and run the required `unit` gate on the pushed correction.

executed_verification: The CLI transcript records the guarded push of 8f8f83ee61ee088412cb24eb2669d2dc1df6aa1d and the pinned controller starting `verify --gate unit`. The candidate-bound receipt records exit 0, an unchanged worktree and 659.4 seconds. The log matches its recorded SHA-256 and reports 256 tests run with one live smoke test skipped.

The candidate gate passed the headless fixtures for rejected verdict and receipt posts, publication of a PR-safe replacement, partial-request withdrawal through handoff, remote edit and deletion detection, and replay of an older amendment file.

The transcript also records 52 focused tests passing before the candidate commit. In a separate handoff-reopen fixture, the candidate gate log prints the retired receipt `final-status-24d0760809` under `pending_publications`.
inspected: The pinned mission and owner guidance, repository instructions, full feature diff, correction commit, prior findings ledger, developer report, CLI transcript, gate receipt and gate log.
The controller's amendment admission, publication retirement, archive, remote readiness and status paths, their behavior tests, both developer prompts, the reviewer prompt and the operator playbook.
limitations: The review used the supplied execution records in the read-only snapshot. The behavior fixtures use real Git repositories, controller state and archive commits with simulated model and GitHub boundaries.
The supplemental live-model gates were not run. Delivery of the eventual handoff notification in the launching conversation is a supervisor duty.
required_gaps: R3-F1 requires accurate status output for settled verdicts and receipts retired by an amendment, with assertions in the headless fixtures.
source_inspection_only: The headless rejected-POST fixtures establish that the verdict and receipt become `superseded`. Their continued appearance in amendment status follows directly from the filter at line 4392. Those fixtures do not assert the returned list for either key.

acceptance_ids: B. Apply at the next safe boundary, without re-enrollment
B. Both roles receive the same effective instructions
findings.actual: `retire_verdict` and `retire_receipts` mark the old publication `superseded`. `send` treats that state as terminal, but `status` excludes only `posted` and `withdrawn`. The retired `r01-review` or `final-status-…` key therefore stays in `pending_publications` after its correction has posted.
findings.blocking_rationale: The supervisor can report outstanding public work, or wait for it to clear, even though the controller has settled the amendment and will never send that publication.
findings.expected: Once retirement and its correction are settled, status omits the retired key. Any part whose delivery is still uncertain remains visible.
findings.requested_correction: Use the same distinction between settled publication states and unresolved POST outcomes that guidance admission already uses.
findings.requested_evidence: In the existing failed-verdict and failed-first-receipt amendment fixtures, inspect status after the correction posts and assert that each retired key is absent. Also confirm that a part with `posting_since` and no confirmed comment ID remains listed.
findings.title: Status lists retired verdicts and handoff receipts as pending
findings.trigger: Apply an amendment after definitive rejection of a verdict POST or the first handoff-receipt POST, then inspect the enrollment's status.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The two candidate-bound fixtures confirm the public correction names the affected round and commit. A rejected verdict leads to withdrawal of the posted request. A rejected first receipt leads to correction of the ready verdict without a reopened-handoff notice. Neither path launches another reviewer.

The refusal fixture checks unchanged state after the unsafe submission, then publishes a safe replacement in the same enrollment. It verifies the replacement text, revision 1 and cumulative document digest in the posted request.

The multipart fixture reaches a current handoff with one delivered part archived, the unsent suffix withdrawn and the request absent from pending publications. Editing or deleting the delivered part makes remote verification identify `r01-request`.

Replay detection checks the saved path and message digest across all revisions. After conflicting amendments A and B, retrying A's original file preserves the state bytes, call count and selection of B. A newly saved file containing A's words is accepted as revision 3.

summary.delivered_behavior: Authenticated reviewer continuations reach resumed and fresh developer sessions. Cumulative owner amendments reach both roles, require a fresh report and preserve the enrollment's findings and expenditure. The fixtures exercise publication, archival and remote handoff verification.
remaining_owner_review: After a verified handoff on [draft PR #6](https://github.com/howardreith/development-process/pull/6), the owner decides whether to accept and install the reviewed controller and whether to activate it for any existing enrollment between runs.
summary.scope_reviewed: The complete continuation and owner-amendment mission at the final checkpoint, with the correction review focused on the four pending findings and the publication states their fixes produce.
